video_title: Private Equity Genius: Lessons That Built a Billion-Dollar Firm
gist: Joe Lonsdale interviews Geoff Rehnert, co-founder of Bain Capital's early team and of middle-market PE firm Audax Group (captioned 'ODAX'), on Bain Capital's 100%+ IRR origins, Audax's recovery from early dot-com-era overreach (Indian Motorcycle, Artisan Entertainment), its systematized buy-and-build machine (1,500+ add-ons), its fast-growing private credit arm (just closed a $10B fund, 30B+ AUM, minimal SaaS/AI stress) and AI deployment across portfolio companies; the back half covers his Miles for Military nonprofit.

themes.theme: Bain Capital origins and early PE returns

insights.claim: Bain Capital launched in 1984 with a $37M fund, the largest first-time fund in venture/LBO at a time when the entire venture capital and leveraged buyout industry managed only about $1.7B.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Illustrates how small and nascent the PE asset class was four decades ago versus today's scale.

insights.claim: Bain Capital's first several funds averaged over 200% IRR on realized deals, and when Rehnert left in 1999 the IRR including unrealized deals at cost was still over 100%.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Benchmark for early-era PE returns that are unlikely to be replicated in today's crowded market.

insights.claim: Bain Capital's founding thesis was to apply Bain & Company strategy-consulting skills to companies it owned, earning equity returns on its own and investors' capital instead of selling fees for services.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Operational value creation, not just financial engineering, was the original PE edge.
insights.quote: rather than sell fees for services, we were going to invest our own capital and our investors capital and generate equity returns

insights.claim: Bain Capital's first leveraged buyout, Calumet Coach (mobile CT/MRI units shared across hospitals), was bought at a low multiple with leverage and sold 2.5 years later for 35x, turning $1M into $35M and returning almost the entire fund.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Shared-services models bought cheaply with leverage can produce outsized returns.
insights.quote: We invested a million dollars and wound up generating 35 million.

insights.claim: Rehnert quipped that AI returns look great on paper but are largely yet to be realized, implying the exit/cash realization of AI investments remains the key open question.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Paper gains in AI portfolios still need liquidity events to prove out.
insights.quote: The AI returns look great on paper right now.

insights.claim: Audax targets the middle market, which has grown from companies with ~$100M revenue, $10-20M EBITDA and $50-100M enterprise value in the early days to essentially anything under ~$1B purchase price today; Audax now mostly buys companies with roughly $40-150M of EBITDA as multiples have expanded.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Defines the deal size band where relationship-driven sourcing and operational change still matter.

insights.claim: Audax's early overreach at the peak of the dot-com bubble (Artisan Entertainment after The Blair Witch Project, a venture fund, a mezzanine fund) spread the team too thin and led to losses on Indian Motorcycle; the lesson was to focus on a distinctive competence: middle-market LBOs of understandable, defensible businesses.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Manager-selection lens: favor firms with focused strategies and teams tested by early failures.
insights.quote: put all your eggs in one basket and watch that basket

insights.claim: Audax has done more than 1,500 add-on acquisitions after deciding to become the best in the industry at buy-and-build, supported by tracked time, specialized deal-sourcing and financing teams, and a 70+ person portfolio support group.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Scaled, systematized roll-up capability is a durable edge in middle-market PE.

insights.claim: By building an in-house legal team for repeatable add-on work, Audax cut average outside legal costs from as much as ~$500K on $2-4M acquisitions to about $20K per add-on, making small, labor-intensive add-ons economic.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Process industrialization unlocks small-deal roll-up economics competitors can't match.
insights.quote: we were able to bring our average outside legal cost down to about $20,000 per add-on acquisition

insights.claim: Audax's long-standing time tracking and early knowledge-management system are, in Rehnert's view, a real moat that is becoming more valuable with AI because it gives the firm years of proprietary data.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Proprietary operating data is an AI-era advantage for scaled PE firms over smaller sponsors.
insights.quote: it's a real moat around our our business

insights.claim: Rehnert argues private equity is net positive because it aligns ownership and control, solving the agency problem of large public companies, and that Audax's portfolio analyses show strong organic growth and net job creation.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Pushback on the political narrative against PE; relevant to regulatory risk for the sector.

insights.claim: Audax just closed a $10B private credit fund and its credit business is now well north of $30B (private equity ~$20B); it runs a hold-to-maturity, non-distressed, diversified strategy with extraordinarily low loss rates.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Institutional demand for direct lending remains strong despite retail private-credit fears.
insights.quote: we just closed a $10 billion private credit fund

insights.claim: Rehnert says the AI-on-SaaS scare that rattled retail private-credit investors has had minimal impact on Audax's book because it had little SaaS exposure, those SaaS borrowers are performing, and its overwhelmingly institutional LPs don't panic.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Distinguish private-credit managers by SaaS exposure and investor base (institutional vs. retail).

insights.claim: Being senior in the capital structure means lenders still get repaid even if AI causes growth at some software businesses to level off: the credit retains value even if the equity is worth less.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Senior debt is a way to stay exposed to software cash flows while hedging AI disruption to equity value.
insights.quote: So the credit is still going to be worth something if the equity is not worth quite as much.

insights.claim: Across its private equity and credit businesses Audax sees roughly 80-90% of all US/North American middle-market transactions, giving it information economies of scale on which businesses and sponsors are good credits.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Deal-flow breadth is a key underwriting advantage for large direct lenders.

insights.claim: Audax's portfolio support group is deploying AI across its middle-market companies with enormous efficiency gains and is already seeing improvement in organic growth, including mining overlapping customers across the portfolio, while also using AI to streamline its own investment process.
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Early evidence AI is lifting margins and organic growth in PE-owned middle-market companies; scaled sponsors benefit most.
insights.quote: We're actually seeing improvement in organic growth.

insights.claim: The military does not pay for junior enlisted personnel to travel home on leave; E1-E4 (about 450,000 of a 2M-strong military) earn in the low $20,000s, so many go two to four years without seeing family; Miles for Military flies them home in exchange for 25+ volunteer hours (flights grew from 49 to 540 to a 5,000 goal this year).
insights.speaker: Geoff Rehnert (Audax Group)
insights.so_what: Philanthropy segment; corporate partners include Empower and Wyndham Hotels.
